title: Primary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease with a Mediterranean Diet Supplemented with Extra-Virgin Olive Oil or Nuts
headline: A Mediterranean diet with olive oil cut major heart events by about 30%
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 7,447 adults at high cardiovascular risk to a Mediterranean diet with extra-virgin olive oil, a Mediterranean diet with mixed nuts, or a low-fat control diet, and followed them for a median of 4.8 years. The olive-oil group had about 31% fewer heart attacks, strokes, and cardiovascular deaths than the control group. This is strong evidence because participants were randomly assigned to groups. The original 2013 paper was retracted and republished in 2018 after randomization irregularities at some sites were corrected; the corrected analysis preserved the main findings. (Hazard Ratio: 0.69, 95% CI 0.53–0.91, p=0.009)
intervention: Mediterranean diet with extra-virgin olive oil
intervention_description: Traditional Mediterranean diet plus at least 4 tablespoons per day of extra-virgin olive oil, provided free to participants
population: adults ages 55 to 80 at high cardiovascular risk
outcome_name: Major cardiovascular events (MI, stroke, or CV death)

title: Preventive effect of eccentric training on acute hamstring injuries in men's soccer: a cluster-randomized controlled trial
headline: The Nordic hamstring exercise cut new soccer hamstring injuries by 60%
summary: Researchers randomly assigned 50 Danish soccer teams (942 male players, 461 in the Nordic group and 481 in the control group) to either add the Nordic hamstring exercise to their training, or to continue training as usual, and tracked injuries across one season. Players doing the Nordic exercise had 60% fewer new hamstring injuries and 85% fewer recurrent injuries. This is strong evidence because teams were randomly assigned to groups. A 2019 meta-analysis of 15 studies and 8,459 athletes confirmed the effect: programmes that include the Nordic hamstring exercise roughly halve the rate of hamstring injuries (pooled risk ratio 0.49, 95% CI 0.32–0.74, p=0.0008). (Rate Ratio: 0.40, p<0.001)
intervention_description: 10-week supervised eccentric hamstring training program added to standard soccer training, then once weekly during the season
population: Danish male professional and amateur soccer players
